S
 Senior Public Prosecutor
 This Bail Application Having Come Up For Admission On
08.11.2024, The Court On The Same Day Passed The Following:
 2024:Ker:83438
B.A No. 8224 Of 2024 2
 Dated this the 8th day of November, 2024

Order 
The application is filed under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, by the sole accused in Crime No. 882/2024 of the Thrissur West Police Station, Thrissur, which is registered against him for allegedly committing the offences punishable under Sections 342, 294(b),
506, 323, 376 and 201 of the Indian Penal Code.

The petitioner was remanded to judicial custody on 15.08.2024.
2.

The prosecution case, in brief, is that; one day between 10 and 15th of May 2023, the accused wrongfully confined the survivor in a class room at Thrissur Kerala Varma College, and after causing hurt to her, he undressed and committed rape on her.
The accused also uttered obscene words and intimidated the survivor, saying that if she disclosed the incident to anyone, he would murder her.
Thus, the accused has 2024:KER:83438 committed the above offences.
3. Heard; Sri. S. Rajeev, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, Smt. Seetha.
S, the learned Senior Public Prosecutor and Sri. N.U. Harikrishna, the learned counsel appearing for the survivor.
4. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is innocent of the accusations levelled against him.
There is no material to substantiate the petitioner's culpability in the crime.
The petitioner and the survivor had a consensual relationship.

Although the alleged incident occurred between 10 and 15th of May 2023, Annexure-1 FIR is registered only on 12.08.2024, after a delay of one year and three months, which proves the falsity and frivolity in the crime.
Annexure A4 communication between the survivor and the petitioner would evidently prove that they had a consensual relationship.
By no stretch of imagination can the offence under Section 376 be attributed against the petitioner.
The petitioner is a 26 2024:KER:83438 year old student without any criminal antecedents.

In any given case, the petitioner has been in judicial custody for the last 84 days, the investigation in the case is complete, the medical examinations have been conducted, and the charge sheet has been filed.
Hence, the application may be allowed.
5. The learned Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel for the intervenor seriously opposed the application.
They submitted that the petitioner had committed a very serious offence by committing rape as well as hurting the survivor.
If the petitioner is enlarged on bail, there is every likelihood of him intimidating the survivor and tampering with evidence.
Hence, the application may be dismissed.

sentences.text: The prosecution allegation is that, between 10 and 15th May 2023, the petitioner committed rape on the survivor.
On a perusal of the records, it is evident that the survivor lodged Annexure-1 FIR on 12.08.2024, that is after one year and three months.

Even though the 2024:KER:83438 survivor has a case that, immediately after the incident, she suffered a psychological breakdown and was being treated by a psychiatrist, these are matters to be investigated and decided after trial.

7. On an appreciation of the materials on record and the allegations made in the FIR and the communication between the parties, prima facie, I find that the relationship between the parties is consensual in nature.
The fact remains that the petitioner has been in judicial custody for the last 84 days, the investigation in the case is complete, and the medical examinations have been conducted.
Admittedly, the petitioner does not have any criminal antecedents.
8. In Vishnu vs. State of Kerala [2023 (4) KHC 1] this Court after scrutinising all the earlier decisions on the point has made a clear distinction between rape and consensual sex.

entities.text: Vishnu vs. State of Kerala [2023 (4) KHC 1]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is held that unless there is an allegation or proof that the accused has given a false promise to marry the victim,
the offence of rape cannot 2024:KER:83438 be attributed.

In a case where a married woman has consensual sex with a man knowing that he is married, there cannot be an inducement of the promise of marriage, and consequentially the offence under Section 376 will not be attracted.

The same legal proposition is reiterated by this Court in X. vs. State of Kerala [2022 KHC 296].
9.

entities.text: X. vs. State of Kerala [2022 KHC 296]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Recently, in Manish Sisodia v. Directorate of Enforcement [2024 INSC 595] the Honourable Supreme Court has observed that, over a period of time, the trial courts and the High Courts have forgotten a very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia v. Directorate of Enforcement [2024 INSC 595]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From its experience, it appears that the trial courts and the High Courts attempt to play safe in matters of grant of bail.
The principle that bail is the rule and refusal is an exception is, at times, followed in breach.

On account of non-grant of bail even in straight forward open and shut cases, the Honourable Supreme Court is flooded with huge number of bail 2024:KER:83438 petitions thereby adding to the huge pendency.
It is high time that the trial courts and the High Courts recognize the principle that "bail is the rule and jail is an exception.

10. After bestowing my anxious consideration to the facts, the rival submissions made across the Bar, and the materials placed on record, particularly on comprehending the fact that the petitioner has been in judicial custody for the last 84 days, the investigation in the case is complete, medical examinations have been conducted, the charge sheet has been filed, and the petitioner does not have any criminal antecedents, I am of the firm view that the petitioner is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
Hence, I am inclined to allow the bail application, but subject to stringent conditions.
If he has no passport, he shall file an affidavit to the effect before the court below on the date of execution of the bond;

(v) In case of violation of any of the conditions mentioned above, the jurisdictional court shall be empowered to consider the application for cancellation of bail, if any filed, and pass orders on the same, in 2024:KER:83438 accordance with law.
(vi) Applications for deletion/modification of the bail conditions shall be moved and entertained by the jurisdictional court.

(vii) Needless to mention, it would be well within the powers of the Investigating Officer to investigate the matter and, if necessary, to effect recoveries on the information, if any, given by the petitioner even while the petitioner is on bail as laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi) and another [2020 (1) KHC 663].
(viii) The observations made in this order are only for the purpose of considering the application and the same shall not be construed as an expression on the merits of the case, which shall be decided by the competent Court.
Sd/-
